nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong tropical sun drives growth, but little of it reaches the forest floor under the tall, dense canopy.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Very wet conditions on the Osa Peninsula keep the lowland forest green and swell the rivers and lagoons.

nodes.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
nodes.desc: Nutrients released from dead leaves, fruit and animals are taken up again by roots in the litter layer.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria and litter insects
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit, dung and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit through much of the year in tropical forests and are eaten by many monkeys, birds and other animals.

nodes.name: Black palm
nodes.desc: A spiny lowland palm of Pacific Central America whose large seeds are eaten and buried by forest rodents.

nodes.name: Heliconia
nodes.desc: Large-leaved herbs of forest openings and edges, common in the lowlands of Costa Rica.

nodes.name: Seasonvine
nodes.desc: A climbing vine whose fruit and foliage are eaten by several forest animals.

nodes.name: Central American agouti
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal here; this rodent eats fruit and seeds and buries some, helping to spread trees.

nodes.name: Lowland paca
nodes.desc: A large nocturnal rodent that eats fruit, seeds and leaves; illegal hunting has reduced it in the region.

nodes.name: Baird's tapir
nodes.desc: Endangered browser that eats leaves, twigs and fruit and sometimes passes seeds intact. Only jaguars and large crocodiles can kill adults.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: Pig-like forest herbivore that eats fruit, seeds, roots and vines, and is a staple prey of cats.

nodes.name: Geoffroy's spider monkey
nodes.desc: Canopy fruit specialist that moves widely to find ripe fruit, spreading seeds as it goes.

nodes.name: Scarlet macaw
nodes.desc: Eats fruit, nuts, seeds and flowers high in the canopy; the park holds Costa Rica's largest population.

nodes.name: Green iguana
nodes.desc: A tree-climbing lizard that eats leaves, flowers and fruit and is eaten by snakes, birds and cats.

nodes.name: Terciopelo
nodes.desc: A large pit viper that ambushes rodents and lizards on the forest floor.

nodes.name: Ocelot
nodes.desc: A medium-sized cat that hunts agoutis, pacas, small peccaries and other mammals, mostly at night.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: Common scavenger that feeds on carcasses and also takes small animals.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Soaring scavenger that finds carrion, including dead peccaries and reptiles.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: Largest cat of the Americas; takes peccaries, agoutis, pacas, tapirs and even large birds. Hunting has reduced it here.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: A widespread big cat that hunts deer, peccaries and other mammals in the forest.

nodes.name: American crocodile
nodes.desc: Large crocodiles in rivers and lagoons can kill adult tapirs; the species lives in the Sirena and nearby rivers.
